# Overview

The following datasets will be used to create a Bioavailability Master Spreadsheet which will have tabs according to the BLM assumptions considered (HA 10% Closed System, HA 10% Open System, and HA 80% Closed System)

1.  **Clean WaDE Synoptic Survey dataset** (WaDE_Synoptic_Summary_Clean.xlsx)

Variables selected: sample ID, site, date, inherent characteristics, developed land cover, BLM predictors.

2.  **WaDE Synoptic Survey dataset** (WaDE_Synoptic_Summary.xlsx, "SITE INFO" tab)

Variables selected: network, regime, upstream distance from main stem, elevation, relative elevation, and developed land cover by site

3.  **BLM Speciation Mode** (Zn_Speciation.det.xlsx)

Variables selected: free ion, biotic ligand (BL) bound elements, inorganic complexes, and organic complexes.

4.  **BLM Toxicity Mode** (Zn acute toxicity.det.xlsx and Zn chronic toxicity.det.xlsx)

Variable selected: total Zn concentration to cause certain type of toxicity to the given organism

```{r}

WaDE_Synoptic_Summary_Clean <- read_excel("C:/Users/q4q/OneDrive - Oak Ridge National Laboratory/Research/Bioavailability Project/BLM_spatial_assessmt/WaDE Dataset Cleaning/WaDE_Synoptic_Summary_Clean.xlsx")
```

Inspect the structure

```{r}
str(WaDE_Synoptic_Summary_Clean)
```

Select sample ID, site, date, flow regime, flow state, developed land cover, BLM predictors

```{r}

bio_ms <- WaDE_Synoptic_Summary_Clean %>%

    Mg_uM,

    Cl_uM,
    DIC_uM,

head(bio_ms)
```

## 2. WaDE Synoptic Survey

Import the original (pre-cleaning) WaDE Synoptic Survey dataset "SITE_INFO" tab for inherent characteristics and developed land use by site.

```{r}
library(readxl)

WaDE_Site_Info <- read_excel("C:/Users/q4q/OneDrive - Oak Ridge National Laboratory/Research/Bioavailability Project/BLM_spatial_assessmt/WaDE Dataset Cleaning/WaDE_Synoptic_Summary.xlsx", 
    sheet = "SITE INFO")

head(WaDE_Site_Info)
```

Inspect the structure

```{r}
str(WaDE_Site_Info)
```

From WaDE_Site_Info we'll select network, regime, elevation, relative elevation, upstream distance from main stem, and developed land cover by site and apply it to all samples by site

```{r}
library(dplyr)

bio_ms <- bio_ms %>%
  left_join(
    WaDE_Site_Info %>%
      rename(
        Elevation_m = `elevation (m) (USGS 3DEP)`,
        Relative_elevation_m = `Relative elevation from main stem (m)`,
        Upstream_from_main_stem_km = `Upstream of EFK_KM`,
        Developed_lulc       = `lulc_developed_%`
      ) %>%
      dplyr::select(
        Site,
        Network,
        Elevation_m,
        Relative_elevation_m,
        Upstream_from_main_stem_km,
        Developed_lulc
      ),
    by = "Site"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Elevation_m = as.numeric(Elevation_m),
    Relative_elevation_m = as.numeric(Relative_elevation_m),
    Developed_lulc       = as.numeric(Developed_lulc),
    Upstream_from_main_stem_km = as.numeric(Upstream_from_main_stem_km)
  ) %>%
   relocate(
    Network,
    Elevation_m,
    Relative_elevation_m,
    Upstream_from_main_stem_km,
    Developed_lulc,
    .after = Flow_state
  )

# check
head(bio_ms)
```

Inspect the structure again

```{r}
str(bio_ms)
```

## 3. BLM Speciation Mode

If you haven't already, convert the Zn_Speciation.det.xlsx to the newest Excel Workbook version before importing them.

Import dataset

```{r}
library(readxl)

Zn_Speciation_ha10_cs <- read_excel("C:/Users/q4q/OneDrive - Oak Ridge National Laboratory/Research/Bioavailability Project/BLM_spatial_assessmt/Zinc/1. Running BLM/Data outputs/Speciation Mode/Zn_speciation_ha10_cs.det.xlsx")

head(Zn_Speciation_ha10_cs)
```

Clean dataset

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)

Zn_Speciation_ha10_cs_clean <- Zn_Speciation_ha10_cs %>%
  # 1) Drop rows 1–3
  slice(-(1:3)) %>%
  
  # 2) Set first remaining row as column names
  { 
    nm <- as.character(.[1, ])
    nm <- make.unique(nm)
    out <- .[-1, ]
    names(out) <- nm
    out
  } %>%
  
  # 3) Remove units row (now the first row)
  slice(-1) %>%
  
  # 4) Rename ID columns
  rename(
    Sample_ID = `Site Label`,
    Site      = `Sample Label`
  ) %>%
  
  # 5) Clean Sample_ID and convert others to numeric
  mutate(
    Sample_ID = str_extract(Sample_ID, "WaDE_\\d+"),
    across(-c(Sample_ID, Site), ~ as.numeric(str_replace_all(.x, '"', "")))
  )


# Preview
head(Zn_Speciation_ha10_cs_clean)

# Sanity check: make sure Sample_ID matches to that of the Bioavailability Master Spreadsheet called bio_ms (should be 386)

Zn_Speciation_ha10_cs_clean %>%
  inner_join(
    Zn_Speciation_ha10_cs_clean %>% 
      dplyr::select(Sample_ID),
    by = "Sample_ID"
  ) %>%
  summarise(n_matched = n())
```

Select variables, add a suffix indicating their units, and add to bio_ms

## 4. BLM Toxicity Mode

### i. Chronic

Import the Zn Toxicity on Zn_chronic_toxicity.det.xlsx

```{r}
library(readxl)

Zn_chronic_toxicity <- read_excel("C:/Users/q4q/OneDrive - Oak Ridge National Laboratory/Research/Bioavailability Project/BLM_spatial_assessmt/Zinc/1. Running BLM/Data outputs/Toxicity Mode/Zn_chronic_toxicity.det.xlsx")

head(Zn_chronic_toxicity)
```

Data cleaning

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)

Zn_chronic_toxicity_clean <- Zn_chronic_toxicity %>%
  # 1) Drop rows 1–3
  slice(-(1:3)) %>%
  
  # 2) Set first remaining row as column names (and make them unique)
  {
    nm <- as.character(.[1, ])
    nm <- make.unique(nm)
    out <- .[-1, ]
    names(out) <- nm
    out
  } %>%
  
  # 3) Remove units row (now the first row)
  slice(-1) %>%
  
  # 4) Rename ID columns
  rename(
    Sample_ID = `Site Label`,
    Site      = `Sample Label`
  ) %>%
  
  # 5) Clean Sample_ID + strip quotes + convert everything else to numeric
  mutate(
    Sample_ID = str_extract(Sample_ID, "WaDE_\\d+"),
    across(-c(Sample_ID, Site), ~ as.numeric(str_replace_all(.x, '"', "")))
  )

# Preview
head(Zn_chronic_toxicity_clean)

# Sanity check: match count vs Bioavailability Master Spreadsheet (bio_ms)
bio_ms %>%
  inner_join(
    Zn_chronic_toxicity_clean %>% dplyr::select(Sample_ID),
    by = "Sample_ID"
  ) %>%
  summarise(n_matched = dplyr::n())
```

Select the T.Zn variable (total amount of Zn to cause the toxicity to the organism) and add to bio_ms

```{r}
library(dplyr)

bio_ms_ha10_cs <- bio_ms_ha10_cs %>%
  left_join(
    Zn_chronic_toxicity_clean %>%
      dplyr::rename(
        Zn_chronic_tox_M = T.Zn
      ) %>%
      dplyr::select(
        Sample_ID,
        Zn_chronic_tox_M
      ),
    by = "Sample_ID"
  )


# Make sure they're numeric
zn_new_vars <- c("Zn_chronic_tox_M")

# Convert them to numeric
bio_ms_ha10_cs <- bio_ms_ha10_cs %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(zn_new_vars), ~ as.numeric(.)))

# Check
str(bio_ms_ha10_cs)
```

## 5. Export to Bioavailability Master Spreadsheet

Since we're saving the data from BLM run as a **closed system assuming HA at 10%**, we'll save it to the Bioavailability Master Spreadsheet into a tab called HA 10% Closed System:

```{r}
library(openxlsx)

file_path <- "Bioavailability_Master_Spreadsheet.xlsx"

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Create workbook if file does NOT exist
# ---------------------------------------------------------
if (!file.exists(file_path)) {
  
  wb <- createWorkbook()
  addWorksheet(wb, "HA 10% Closed System")
  writeData(wb, "HA 10% Closed System", bio_ms_ha10_cs)
  saveWorkbook(wb, file_path, overwrite = TRUE)

} else {

  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  # 2. If the file EXISTS, load it and add/overwrite the sheet
  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  wb <- loadWorkbook(file_path)

  # Add sheet if missing
  if (!"HA 10% Closed System" %in% names(wb)) {
    addWorksheet(wb, "HA 10% Closed System")
  }

  # Write/overwrite data in that sheet
  writeData(wb, "HA 10% Closed System", bio_ms_ha10_cs)

  # Save
  saveWorkbook(wb, file_path, overwrite = TRUE)
}
```

## 2. Export to Bioavailability Master Spreadsheet

Since we're saving the data from BLM run as a **open system assuming HA at 10%**, we'll save it to the Bioavailability Master Spreadsheet into a tab called HA 10% Closed System:

```{r}
library(openxlsx)

file_path <- "Bioavailability_Master_Spreadsheet.xlsx"

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Create workbook if file does NOT exist
# ---------------------------------------------------------
if (!file.exists(file_path)) {
  
  wb <- createWorkbook()
  addWorksheet(wb, "HA 10% Open System")
  writeData(wb, "HA 10% Open System", bio_ms_ha10_os)
  saveWorkbook(wb, file_path, overwrite = TRUE)

} else {

  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  # 2. If the file EXISTS, load it and add/overwrite the sheet
  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  wb <- loadWorkbook(file_path)

  # Add sheet if missing
  if (!"HA 10% Open System" %in% names(wb)) {
    addWorksheet(wb, "HA 10% Open System")
  }

  # Write/overwrite data in that sheet
  writeData(wb, "HA 10% Open System", bio_ms_ha10_os)

  # Save
  saveWorkbook(wb, file_path, overwrite = TRUE)
}
```

Clean datasets

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(readxl)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Cleaning function
# ------------------------------------------------------------
clean_blm_speciation <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    # Drop rows 1–3
    slice(-(1:3)) %>%
    
    # Set first remaining row as column names
    {
      nm <- as.character(.[1, ])
      nm <- make.unique(nm)
      out <- .[-1, ]
      names(out) <- nm
      out
    } %>%
    
    # Remove units row
    slice(-1) %>%
    
    # Rename ID columns
    rename(
      Sample_ID = `Site Label`,
      Site      = `Sample Label`
    ) %>%
    
    # Drop rows below this are populated with NA
    slice(1:386) %>%
    
    # Clean Sample_ID and convert all other columns to numeric
    mutate(
      Sample_ID = str_extract(Sample_ID, "WaDE_\\d+"),
      across(-c(Sample_ID, Site), ~ as.numeric(str_replace_all(.x, '"', "")))
    )
}


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Apply cleaning function to all 7 files
# ------------------------------------------------------------
Zn_Speciation_ha20_cs_clean <- clean_blm_speciation(Zn_Speciation_ha20_cs)
Zn_Speciation_ha30_cs_clean <- clean_blm_speciation(Zn_Speciation_ha30_cs)
```

Create a dataframe with HA_content, Sample_ID, TBL-Zn (mol/kg)

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Function to extract TBL Zn and add HA content
# ------------------------------------------------------------
extract_tbl_zn <- function(df, ha_value) {
  df %>%
    mutate(
      HA_content = ha_value,
      TBL_Zn_mol_kg = `BL-Zn` + `BL-ZnOH`
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(Sample_ID, HA_content, TBL_Zn_mol_kg)
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Build final stacked dataset
# ------------------------------------------------------------
Zn_TBL_by_HA <- bind_rows(
  extract_tbl_zn(Zn_Speciation_ha10_cs_clean, 10),
  extract_tbl_zn(Zn_Speciation_ha20_cs_clean, 20),
  extract_tbl_zn(Zn_Speciation_ha30_cs_clean, 30),
  extract_tbl_zn(Zn_Speciation_ha40_cs_clean, 40),
  extract_tbl_zn(Zn_Speciation_ha50_cs_clean, 50),
  extract_tbl_zn(Zn_Speciation_ha60_cs_clean, 60),
  extract_tbl_zn(Zn_Speciation_ha70_cs_clean, 70),
  extract_tbl_zn(Zn_Speciation_ha80_cs_clean, 80)
)

head(Zn_TBL_by_HA)
str(Zn_TBL_by_HA)
```

## 2. Export to Bioavailability Master Spreadsheet

```{r}
library(openxlsx)

file_path <- "Bioavailability_Master_Spreadsheet.xlsx"

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Create workbook if file does NOT exist
# ---------------------------------------------------------
if (!file.exists(file_path)) {
  
  wb <- createWorkbook()
  addWorksheet(wb, "HA 10-80%")
  writeData(wb, "HA 10-80%", Zn_TBL_by_HA)
  saveWorkbook(wb, file_path, overwrite = TRUE)

} else {

  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  # 2. If the file EXISTS, load it and add/overwrite the sheet
  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  wb <- loadWorkbook(file_path)

  # Add sheet if missing
  if (!"HA 10-80%" %in% names(wb)) {
    addWorksheet(wb, "HA 10-80%")
  }

  # Write/overwrite data in that sheet
  writeData(wb, "HA 10-80%", Zn_TBL_by_HA)

  # Save
  saveWorkbook(wb, file_path, overwrite = TRUE)
}
```
